problem: The cinema doors opened 15 minutes before the Saturday morning cartoon show. By then 64 tickets had been sold, 29 of them to adults and the rest to children. How many children's tickets had been sold?

follow_ups.question: Once the show began, 18 more children turned up and bought tickets at the door. How many children watched the cartoon show?

problem: Mrs. Okafor's class went to see a film about whales on Thursday. Twenty-six pupils rode on the first minibus and 19 rode on the second. What was the total number of pupils at the cinema?

follow_ups.question: After the film, 7 pupils were collected by their parents and the others walked back to school together. How many walked back?

problem: The little screen at the Rialto shows the same film twice every Friday, once at four o'clock and again at seven. Last Friday 37 people came to the early showing and 48 to the late one. The film is 95 minutes long. How many people saw it that Friday?

follow_ups.question: On Saturday the two showings had 56 people between them. How many people saw the film on Friday and Saturday?
Sunday had just one showing, and 63 people watched it. What is the total for the whole weekend?
Of everyone who came that weekend, 79 were children. How many were adults?

problem: Aiko's birthday treat was a trip to the cinema. Before the film began, she filled a tray with 14 cups of lemonade and 12 cups of orange juice for her guests. How many cups were on the tray?

follow_ups.question: During the film the guests drank 17 cups. How many cups were still full?
In the interval, Aiko poured 6 more cups of lemonade. How many full cups were there then?

problem: Every morning before the first show, Mr. Bao checks all the seats in the cinema. There are 32 seats up in the balcony and 56 seats downstairs. What is the total number of seats he checks each morning?

follow_ups.question: On Tuesday he found chewing gum stuck to 9 of the seats. How many seats were free of gum?

problem: Saturday's matinee at the cinema sold 78 tickets, and the evening show sold 95. Work out how many tickets the cinema sold on Saturday.

follow_ups.question: Sunday's two shows together sold 47 tickets fewer than Saturday's. How many tickets were sold on Sunday?

problem: Lena works at the cinema snack bar. When she arrives at noon, she counts 23 small boxes of popcorn on the shelf and 34 large boxes in the cupboard. What total does she get?

follow_ups.question: By the end of the first film, 25 boxes have been sold. How many boxes are left?
Before the second film, the manager brings up 20 more boxes from the store room. How many boxes does Lena have now?

problem: On Wednesday afternoon, 72 people visited the cinema. Everyone watched either the cartoon or the nature film, and 45 chose the cartoon. How many chose the nature film?

follow_ups.question: The following Wednesday, the nature film had 9 more viewers than this time. How many viewers did it have then?
On that following Wednesday the cartoon drew 40 viewers. How many people came to the cinema that day?

problem: At nine o'clock, an usher set out blankets for the cosy morning screening: 41 blankets along the front rows and 37 along the back rows. Find the number of blankets she set out.
During morning break, 18 children were on the climbing frame and 25 were on the swings. How many children were using these two parts of the playground?

follow_ups.question: When the bell rang, 30 of them went inside. How many were still playing there?
Then 8 more children came out for a late break. How many were on the frame and swings now?
The teacher on duty gives each of those children 2 stickers for sharing nicely. How many stickers does she give out?

problem: There are 35 children on the playground on Friday morning. Some are in the sandpit and the other 16 are playing hopscotch. Find the number of children in the sandpit.

follow_ups.question: After snack time, 7 children left the sandpit for the slide. How many stayed in the sandpit?

problem: Over the summer holiday, painters marked new games on Zara's school playground. They painted 24 hopscotch squares in the morning and 17 in the afternoon. The paint was bright yellow. How many squares did they paint that day?

follow_ups.question: The next day they painted a snail game with 15 squares. How many squares did they paint over the two days?
A storm washed away 6 of the squares. How many squares could still be seen?

problem: The council's plan says the new playground opens on Saturday. The builders used 48 wooden posts for the fence and 76 metal posts for the climbing area. Calculate the number of posts they put in.

follow_ups.question: Each post is held by 2 bolts. How many bolts did the posts need?
On Friday, 15 of those bolts snapped and were replaced with new ones. Counting the replacements, how many bolts were used?
On opening morning, the builders used 37 more bolts to fix the benches. What was the new total of bolts?

problem: The school has 3 playgrounds. Before lunch, 27 younger children played on the big one, and after lunch, 38 older children played there. How many children played on the big playground that day?

follow_ups.question: Of those children, 9 had brought a ball from home. How many had not?

problem: Fewer children than usual came out to the playground at lunch on Tuesday: only 13 girls and 22 boys. What was the number of children outside?
Fifty pieces of chalk came in the box Mr. Haddad opened on Monday for playground drawing. Thirty-two pieces were white. How many were coloured?

follow_ups.question: By Friday the children had worn down 11 of the coloured pieces to nothing. How many coloured pieces remained?

problem: Before going home, the teacher left two bags of balls by the shed: 16 footballs in one and 14 tennis balls in the other. How many balls did she leave by the shed?

follow_ups.question: The next morning, 4 of the tennis balls had gone. How many balls were still there?
At playtime the caretaker found 3 of the missing balls under a bench and put them back. How many balls are there now?
Twenty-one of those balls were taken out to play at lunch. How many stayed by the shed?

problem: How many children went out to the playground at the after-school club on Wednesday, if 40 children came and 23 of them stayed indoors to paint?

follow_ups.question: At four o'clock, 6 of the painters went outside too. How many children were on the playground then?

problem: On Saturday morning Coach Ama counted 52 riders at the skate park, some on skateboards and some on scooters. Thirty-four were skateboarding. Find how many were on scooters.

follow_ups.question: By lunchtime, 9 of the scooter riders had gone home. How many scooter riders were still at the park?

problem: Tomás spent Sunday afternoon covering his skateboard with 30 stickers. He put 12 on top. The others went underneath, where nobody would see them. How many did he stick underneath?
The skate park opened 6 years ago. Today it has 26 ramps and rails. If 11 of them are ramps, what is the number of rails?

follow_ups.question: Next spring the park will add 4 more rails. How many rails will it have then?

problem: A skate contest took place over the weekend, and 96 riders entered. Of these, 38 rode skateboards and 27 rode BMX bikes; the rest rode scooters. It was the busiest weekend the park had ever seen. How many riders were on scooters?

follow_ups.question: On Sunday every scooter rider did 2 runs. How many scooter runs were there?
The judges gave a medal for 15 of those runs. How many runs got no medal?
Late in the afternoon, 8 extra runs were added for a final round. How many scooter runs were there in all?

problem: By Monday evening, the skate shop next to the park had counted its 85 helmets: 47 were blue and the rest were black. What number of helmets were black?

follow_ups.question: On Tuesday a delivery brought 24 more black helmets. How many black helmets did the shop have then?
How many helmets did the shop have in all after the delivery?

problem: Ines practised kickflips for 20 minutes before school and 35 minutes after school. Her board has 4 wheels. How many minutes did she practise that day?

follow_ups.question: On Saturday she practised for 40 minutes more than that. How long did she practise on Saturday?

problem: The skate park's timetable gives 90 minutes to Tuesday's session. The beginners' lesson takes 35 minutes, the ramp lesson takes 25 minutes, and the last part is free skating. How long is the free skating?

follow_ups.question: Thursday's session is 15 minutes longer, but the two lessons stay the same length. How long is free skating on Thursday?
What is the total free skating time over both days?

problem: At the café beside the skate park, which has 8 tables, staff sold 68 drinks before noon and 57 after noon. Work out how many drinks were sold that day.

follow_ups.question: The next day they sold 39 fewer drinks. How many drinks did they sell then?
How many drinks were sold over the two days?

problem: The skate show began at 3 o'clock. Priya counted 45 people watching: 19 sat on the steps and the others stood by the fence. How many people were standing?

follow_ups.question: Halfway through, 8 of the standing people found spaces on the steps. How many were still standing?

problem: School was closed on Tuesday because of snow, so the children on Elm Street spent the morning building snowmen. By lunch they had made 24 snowmen altogether, and 15 had carrot noses. How many snowmen had no carrot nose?

follow_ups.question: After lunch, Mrs. Kowalski brought out 6 more carrots for snowmen without noses. How many snowmen still had no nose?
Later the children built 5 new snowmen, all without noses. How many snowmen were without a nose now?
How many snowmen stood on Elm Street at the end of the day?

problem: Right after breakfast, Wen got ready for the big snowball fight with 36 snowballs. She kept 14 in her bucket and stacked the others in a pile. Her gloves were already soaked. How many snowballs were in the pile?

When the snow day was announced, Jonas and his dad went sledging. Jonas raced down the hill 17 times before lunch and 15 times after lunch. Their sledge is bright red. Can you work out how many rides Jonas took?

follow_ups.question: His dad took 9 fewer rides than Jonas. How many rides did his dad take?
How many rides did the two of them take in total?
Each of Jonas's rides took 2 minutes. How many minutes did Jonas spend riding down the hill?

problem: The corner shop stayed open on the snow day and sold 63 pairs of gloves and mittens by closing time. If 27 pairs were mittens, how many pairs were gloves?

follow_ups.question: The next morning another 14 pairs of gloves were sold. How many pairs of gloves were sold over the two days?

problem: On snowy Wednesday the schoolyard had two snow forts. The fort on the left was built from 28 snow blocks, and the one on the right from 34. How many blocks went into both forts?

follow_ups.question: By Thursday afternoon, 19 of the blocks had melted. How many blocks were still standing?
On Friday the children added 12 fresh blocks. How many blocks did the forts have then?

problem: The secretary must phone 84 families in all to say school is shut for snow. She phones 39 of them before eight o'clock and the others after. How many families does she phone after eight o'clock?
A chart on the classroom wall shows this winter's snow days: five in December and eight in January. What is the total number of snow days on the chart?

follow_ups.question: February brought 4 more snow days. How many snow days did the winter have by the end of February?
On each snow day, the class bird feeder needs 2 cups of seed. How many cups of seed did the feeder need over all those days?

problem: Over 3 snowy days, Fatima gathered pine cones for her snowman family: 21 from the garden and 18 from the park. Find how many pine cones she gathered in all.

follow_ups.question: She used 25 of them as buttons. How many pine cones were not used?
Her brother gave her 16 more pine cones. How many unused pine cones does she have now?

problem: On Saturday morning Eli and his sister Sara cleared snow from the driveway, filling 50 buckets together. Eli filled 28 of them. How many buckets did Sara fill?

follow_ups.question: After lunch Sara filled 13 more buckets. How many buckets has Sara filled that day?

problem: On a wet Monday, 31 umbrellas were standing in the school's umbrella racks. Twelve of them were striped and the rest were plain. The rain did not stop all day. How many umbrellas were plain?
Because it rained all Saturday, Hana stayed in doing jigsaws. She completed a 48-piece jigsaw, then started and finished a 35-piece one before tea. How many pieces did she fit together?

follow_ups.question: Afterwards, 6 pieces of the second jigsaw fell under the sofa. How many pieces of that jigsaw were still on the table?

problem: Class 4's rain gauge collected 95 millimetres of rain over two weeks. In the first week it collected 58 millimetres. How much rain fell in the second week?

follow_ups.question: The third week added 26 millimetres. How much rain fell in the second and third weeks together?

problem: The rain started just after breakfast on Sunday. By lunchtime Freya had spotted 19 puddles in the car park and 23 on the field. What was the total number of puddles she spotted?

follow_ups.question: In the afternoon the sun came out and dried up 15 of them. How many puddles were left?
A shower in the evening made 8 new puddles. How many were there at bedtime?

problem: Rain kept Mr. Adeyemi's class indoors at playtime. Of the 28 children, some played board games while 13 built with blocks. How many played board games?

follow_ups.question: At the next rainy playtime, 4 more children chose board games than this time. How many chose board games then?
At that next rainy playtime, how many children built with blocks?

problem: Wet boots lined the corridor after the morning's downpour, 26 on the bottom rack and 30 on the top rack. Altogether, how many boots were on the racks?
Gabriel and his grandmother waited out a rainy afternoon by baking before dinner. They made 24 oat cookies and 18 ginger cookies. What was the size of their whole batch of cookies?

follow_ups.question: After dinner the family ate 11 cookies. How many cookies were left?

problem: The class trip to the museum was cancelled because of rain, so the 27 pupils watched films instead. The first film lasted 45 minutes and the second lasted 38 minutes. How many minutes of films did they watch?

follow_ups.question: Then they had a 10-minute break. How many minutes had passed since the first film started?
Home time came 7 minutes after the break ended. How many minutes passed from the start of the first film to home time?

problem: The space club meets twice a week. On Tuesday 79 star stickers were handed out, and on Thursday, when fewer pupils came, 68 were handed out. How many stickers were handed out that week?

follow_ups.question: The next week 54 stickers were handed out. How many stickers were handed out over the two weeks?

problem: For the space club's night-sky model, Yusuf spent Wednesday afternoon gluing 33 silver stars and 29 gold stars onto black card. What is the count of stars on the card?

follow_ups.question: On Friday he added 8 paper planets. How many shapes are glued on the card now?

problem: On Friday night the space club has the big telescope for 60 minutes. Ruby gets 25 minutes, Tariq gets 20 minutes, and the club leader uses the time that is left. How long does the club leader get?
During Saturday's launch session, the space club fired 30 paper rockets in all. Seventeen sailed over the fence; how many landed inside the field?

follow_ups.question: Of the rockets inside the field, 4 were bent. How many good rockets were in the field?
The children mended 2 of the bent ones. How many good rockets do they have in the field now?

problem: For Friday's Mars night, the space club ordered 36 juice boxes, 48 packets of crackers and 24 apples. How many snack items did they order?

follow_ups.question: At the end of the night, 18 items had not been eaten. How many were eaten?
The 2 club leaders split the uneaten items equally. How many did each leader take home?

problem: In Monday's session the space club made a poster of all 8 planets. Of the 25 members, 14 drew Saturn and the rest drew Jupiter. How many drew Jupiter?

follow_ups.question: On Wednesday, 3 of the Jupiter artists switched to Saturn. How many Saturn drawings were there then?

problem: The coach to the planetarium set off from school at 9 o'clock. On board were 34 space club members and 6 parents. How many people were on the coach?

follow_ups.question: At the planetarium, 25 pupils from another school joined them for the morning show. How many people watched the show?
Before the afternoon show, 19 of them went to the gift shop. How many stayed in the dome?

problem: Leila keeps a moon diary for the space club. It has 30 pages, and by Friday she had filled 18. How many pages were still empty?

follow_ups.question: Over the weekend she filled 5 more pages. How many empty pages remain?
Her teacher gave her an extra notebook with 20 pages. How many empty pages does she have now?
During the next month she used 9 pages for planet drawings. How many empty pages are left?

problem: Before Thursday's test run, Arjun's robot needs 16 short wires and 12 long wires. In all, how many wires does it need?

follow_ups.question: He already has 9 wires in his box. How many more wires does he need?
His teacher hands him 10 of them. How many wires does Arjun still need to find?

problem: At the start of Monday's meeting, the robotics club's tub held 64 parts, all of them either gears or axles. If 37 parts were gears, how many were axles?
The robotics club meets in Room 6 after school. Its 21 members split into builders and coders, and 13 chose to build. How many chose to code?

follow_ups.question: Next week, 4 builders will switch to coding. How many coders will there be then?

problem: Sofia's robot has to roll 50 centimetres along the test track. It stops after 32 centimetres to turn its head. Its battery light is still glowing green. How far does it still have to roll?

follow_ups.question: For the second test the track is made 15 centimetres longer. How far will the robot have to roll from where it stopped?

problem: The robotics club spent Monday and Tuesday building a robot arm, using 27 screws on Monday and 36 on Tuesday. Everyone wore safety goggles. Find the number of screws that went into the arm.

follow_ups.question: On Wednesday they took out 8 screws that were in the wrong holes. How many screws were still in the arm?
On Thursday they put in 14 new screws. How many screws are in the arm now?
The finished arm needs 80 screws. How many more screws must they add?

problem: Two robotics teams practised for the contest. Team Bolt's robot picked up 87 blocks in its practice runs, and Team Spark's robot picked up 76. The contest is in 5 days. How many blocks did the two robots pick up?

follow_ups.question: Bolt's robot dropped 18 of its blocks. How many blocks did Bolt's robot keep?
Counting the blocks Bolt kept and all of Spark's blocks, what is the total?

problem: For the end-of-term robot show, the club printed 96 tickets for parents and 85 tickets for pupils. Exactly how many tickets were printed?

follow_ups.question: On the evening of the show, 23 tickets were not used. How many tickets were used?

problem: The robotics club's parts drawer holds 75 lights altogether: 26 red, 19 green and the others blue. How many blue lights are in the drawer?

follow_ups.question: On Tuesday the club used 12 blue lights for a robot's eyes. How many blue lights are left?
On Wednesday a parent donated 25 blue lights. How many blue lights are there now?
How many lights of all colours are in the drawer now?

problem: At chess club on Thursday, Noah knocked over the box. A chess set has 32 pieces, and he found 25 of them still on the table. Luckily the board was not damaged. How many pieces had fallen on the floor?

follow_ups.question: He picked up 4 of them before the bell. How many were still on the floor?
How many pieces were back on the table now?

problem: The chess club meets every Tuesday at lunchtime in Room 12. Of its 44 members, 26 are beginners. How many members are not beginners?

follow_ups.question: By spring, 7 beginners had become advanced players. How many advanced players were there then?
How many beginners were left?

problem: A chess tournament filled the whole of Saturday, and 96 games were played. There were 47 games in the morning and 28 in the early afternoon; the rest were played late in the afternoon. How many games were played late in the afternoon?
Over the autumn term, the chess club played 58 matches against other schools and 67 matches among its own members. Find how many matches the club played that term.
By the end of September the chess club had raised 90 dollars for new clocks: 54 dollars from a cake sale and the rest from a sponsored game. How much came from the sponsored game?

follow_ups.question: In October they raised another 48 dollars. How much money do they have now?
A chess clock costs 46 dollars. How many clocks can the club buy with all the money?

problem: Eun-ji solved chess puzzles every day of the holiday: 39 in the first week and 64 in the second week. What is the total number of puzzles she solved?
In the week before the chess final, Marta and Ivan played 20 games altogether, with no draws. Marta won 12 of them. How many did Ivan win?
The giant outdoor chessboard has 64 squares to be painted. The pupils painted 27 on Monday and 19 on Tuesday. Painting is messy work. How many squares are still unpainted?

follow_ups.question: On Wednesday they painted half of the unpainted squares. How many squares did they paint on Wednesday?
How many squares still need paint after Wednesday?
On Thursday a group painted those last squares and then repainted 6 squares that had been smudged. How many squares did Thursday's group paint?

problem: On camp Saturday, the scouts gathered 85 sticks for the campfire. They collected 38 before lunch and 29 after lunch, and found the rest at dusk. How many sticks were found at dusk?

follow_ups.question: That evening the fire burned 40 of the sticks. How many sticks were not burned?
On Sunday morning they used 17 more to cook breakfast. How many sticks were left after breakfast?

problem: Selling biscuits is less fun in the rain, but the scouts still sold 76 boxes on Saturday and 58 on Sunday. Work out how many boxes they sold over the two days.

On the morning of the hike, the leader counted 30 scouts at the gate. Eighteen had brought a water bottle and the rest had forgotten theirs. Birds were singing in the trees. How many scouts had forgotten a bottle?

follow_ups.question: The leader had 8 spare bottles to hand out. How many scouts were still without one?
At the first stop, every scout who had a bottle refilled it 2 times. How many refills was that?
The leader's big jug held enough water for 9 more refills. Counting those too, how many refills could the group make?

problem: Before they left camp on Sunday, the scouts counted their tent pegs: 48 in the big tent bags and 56 in the small ones. How many pegs did they have?
Badge night starts at 7 o'clock every Friday. Last Friday the leaders handed out 45 badges, 27 of them for cooking and the others for knot tying. How many knot-tying badges were handed out?
For summer camp the scouts packed 64 tins of beans and 79 tins of soup. Calculate how many tins went into their packs.

follow_ups.question: During the week at camp they ate 98 tins. How many tins did they bring home?
At home they shared those tins equally among 5 patrols. How many tins did each patrol get?
One patrol gave 6 of its tins to a neighbour. How many tins did that patrol keep?

problem: A three-day scout hike covers 47 kilometres. The scouts walk 18 kilometres on Friday and 15 on Saturday. How far do they walk on Sunday?

follow_ups.question: On Sunday they walk half of that distance before lunch. How many kilometres do they walk before lunch?
Next year the whole hike will be 9 kilometres longer. How long will it be?

problem: The scouts held a car wash on Saturday. Before lunch they washed 22 cars; after lunch another 17 rolled in to be washed. In total, how many cars did they wash?

follow_ups.question: On Sunday they washed 14 cars. How many cars did they wash over the weekend?

problem: The school's recycling drive ran for 3 weeks. Of the 92 bags collected, 47 held plastic and the others held paper. How many bags held paper?
The recycling bin outside the hall is emptied every morning at 8 o'clock. On Tuesday, before it was emptied, it held 60 items: 34 bottles and some cans. How many cans were in it?

follow_ups.question: On Wednesday the bin held 12 more cans than on Tuesday. How many cans did it hold on Wednesday?

problem: The two classes taking part in the recycling drive have 48 children between them. One class has 25 children. How many are in the other class?

follow_ups.question: On Friday every child in the smaller class brought 2 bags of paper. How many bags did that class bring?

problem: Chidi's family put out their recycling on Thursday morning: 9 newspapers and 14 glass jars. How many items did they put out?

follow_ups.question: The collector broke 3 of the jars. How many jars reached the recycling centre safely?

problem: During recycling week, the juniors brought in 87 plastic bottles and the infants brought in 69. How many bottles did the school collect?

follow_ups.question: The recycling centre paid 2 cents for every bottle. How many cents did the school get?
The school spent 95 cents of it on prize stickers. How many cents were left?

problem: Isla sorted 40 items on recycling morning. She put 23 into the blue bin and the rest into the green bin. The green bin smelled of old bananas. How many items went into the green bin?

follow_ups.question: Then she found 5 more items for the green bin under a table. How many items went into the green bin in all?

problem: Sione drives a recycling truck. On Monday his route has 70 bins to empty, and by ten o'clock he has emptied 46. How many bins are still waiting?
Lucas and Amira collected 55 bottle caps between them for the recycling art wall. Lucas found 29. The art wall is in the front hall. How many did Amira find?

follow_ups.question: They glued 40 caps onto the wall on Monday. How many caps did they still have?
On Tuesday Amira brought in 10 more caps. How many caps were waiting to be glued?

problem: Work out how many tins of soup the food bank received this week if 73 arrived on Monday and 58 came on Tuesday.

follow_ups.question: On Wednesday volunteers packed 96 of the tins into parcels. How many tins were not packed?
On Thursday 27 more tins arrived. How many unpacked tins are there now?
If 2 tins go into each parcel, how many parcels can they make from the unpacked tins?

problem: On Friday's shelf check, the food bank had 64 bags of rice and pasta altogether. Thirty-nine were rice. How many bags of pasta were there?

follow_ups.question: Over the weekend, 11 bags of pasta were given out. How many pasta bags remain?

problem: Before the winter holidays, Mr. Ito's class gave 31 cans to the food bank and Ms. Rossi's class gave 27. How many cans did both classes give?
The food bank opens at 10 o'clock on Saturdays. This Saturday, families took home 35 boxes of fruit and 28 boxes of vegetables. How many boxes went home with families?

follow_ups.question: Last Saturday, 9 fewer boxes went home. How many boxes was that?
How many boxes went home on the two Saturdays together?

problem: Rafael, who is 8, helped his aunt at the food bank after school. He stacked 26 cartons of milk and 19 cartons of juice. How many cartons did he stack?

follow_ups.question: His aunt stacked 30 more cartons than he did. How many did she stack?
How many cartons did they stack together?

problem: Before the doors opened on Saturday, volunteers filled the bread shelf with 18 white loaves and 24 brown loaves. The bread was still warm. What was the total number of loaves on the shelf?

follow_ups.question: By noon, 29 loaves had been taken. How many loaves were left on the shelf?

problem: The food bank gave out 50 parcels this week. Families with children received 32 of them, and older people living alone received the rest. How many parcels went to older people?

follow_ups.question: Next week the food bank plans to give 6 more parcels to older people than this week. How many is that?

problem: Gloria's Sunday shift at the food bank lasts 90 minutes. The first 35 minutes are for sorting donations, and the rest is for packing bags. How long does she spend packing?

follow_ups.question: Next Sunday, packing will take 15 minutes less. How long will packing take then?

problem: The post office received 85 letters in all on Monday morning. Of these, 48 were for the town and the rest were for the villages. How many were for the villages?

follow_ups.question: In the afternoon, 16 more letters for the villages arrived. How many village letters came that day?

problem: Kalinda bought stamps on Wednesday: 20 for letters at home and 15 for letters going abroad. How many stamps did she buy?

follow_ups.question: By Friday she had used 12 of them. How many stamps did she have left?
Her brother gave her 7 of his stamps. How many stamps does she have now?

problem: Before noon, the postal worker left 23 letters at houses on Oak Road and 31 at houses on Pine Road. How many letters did she leave on the two roads?
On Tuesday the post office sold 78 first-class stamps and 96 second-class stamps. The queue reached the door all morning. How many stamps did it sell that day?

follow_ups.question: Wednesday's sales were 45 stamps lower than Tuesday's. What were Wednesday's sales?
How many stamps were sold over the two days?

problem: Before the post office closed on Friday, Ravi, the clerk, weighed 27 parcels and 38 large letters. How many items did he weigh?

follow_ups.question: Of those, 14 were sent back because the address was missing. How many were sent on?
On Saturday morning he weighed 9 more parcels. How many items did he weigh over Friday and Saturday?

problem: The post office has 99 parcels to deliver on Monday. The van takes 42 on its morning round and 35 on its afternoon round, and the rest wait until Tuesday. How many parcels wait until Tuesday?

follow_ups.question: On Tuesday 18 new parcels also need delivering. How many parcels go out on Tuesday?

problem: Tomasz kept a list of the post he sent home from his summer trip: 36 postcards, 45 letters and 28 small parcels. How many things did he post?

follow_ups.question: All but 15 of them arrived on time. How many arrived on time?

problem: When the red postbox was emptied at five o'clock, it held 58 letters. Twenty-two were in white envelopes and the rest in brown ones. The postbox is very old and covered in moss. How many letters were in brown envelopes?

follow_ups.question: Half of the brown envelopes were for the same street. How many brown envelopes was that?
The postman found 3 more letters for that street stuck at the bottom of the box. How many letters for that street were there now?
Counting the 3 letters that were stuck, how many letters had been in the postbox?
